newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 17.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Former African National Congress (ANC) leader the Rev Allan Boesak proclaimed his innocence before a tumultuous 1,000-strong crowd of ANC supporters outside Cape Town Airport on Sunday and described his fraud and theft trial as "unjust".

- Government's failure to honour its pledge to "rightsize" the public service has been thrown into harsh relief by the disclosure that nearly 2,000 more posts were abolished last year than were created.

- Super Group finalises negotiations to acquire Bluefin and Alex Carriers, merging the companies in a 267 million rand deal and giving the group control over the largest transport infrastructure and distribution network in sub-Saharan Africa.
- Parliament's welfare committee puts the brakes on the further implementation of a controversial cabinet decision to introduce a flat rate child support benefit after ANC MPs voiced serious concern.

- An urgent amendment to the Truth and Reconciliation Act is expected within the next few weeks to allow the amnesty committee to deal with the more than 5,200 applications already received from perpetrators of human rights violations. Hundreds more applications are expected to be filed before the cut-off date of May 10.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Super Group, the diversified transport group, buys Alex Carriers and Bluefin, the two long-distance African transporters. The purchase price will be settled by issuing 56.3 million new shares at an average price of 4.73 rand each.

- Chris Stals, the governor of the central Reserve Bank, has taken a strongly bullish view of South Africa's economic growth prospects this year, predicting a rate one percentage point above that of the Budget and economists' consensus.

- A rift between Cosatu, the country's largest labour federation, and Tito Mboweni, the labour minister, is widening over an impending general strike to force labour's demands in employment standards legislation proposed by the ministry.

- The Reserve Bank has kept the guidelines for growth in the M3 broad money supply aggregate unchanged at between six percent and 10 percent for the second consecutive year, signalling its determination to force the growth in money supply and credit extension by the banks to lower levels.
SAKE BEELD
- The South African Reserve Bank is not planning to relax its monetary policies this year, bank governor Chris Stals tells parliament.
- The government pledges to single-mindedly hunt down its "ghost workers" this year to save taxpayers hundreds of millions of rand in wasted salaries.
- Eight of South Africa's nine premiers met in Johannesburg on Friday to network with a group of 14 international bankers on issues related to economic development.
THE STAR
- Former deputy president F.W. de Klerk, under renewed criticism over the past murders of MK operatives in KwaZulu-Natal, blames the killings on "mavericks" within the security forces.
- Three years into the drafting of the government's official affirmative action policy, whites are still getting the best jobs and are among the highest paid employees in the country.
- Former activist Allan Boesak says the whole anti-apartheid struggle will be on trial with him over charges that he misappropriated more than one million rand in donor funds.
